verdicts.decision_note: The client explicitly requires a system-layout artifact for the initial prototype.
The client confirms that the system design will be developed as a CAD artifact.
The source defines dispensing and splash-control behavior, not a change to the system-layout or CAD deliverable; narrower product Requirements are better targets.
The source approves motor speed and mixing behavior but does not require the asserted CAD accommodation; the variable-speed and splash-control Requirements are narrower targets.
The clauses establish independently testable bowl-removal, whisk-release, mixing-position, and splash-control behaviors already represented by narrower Requirements.
The exchange makes the completed system layout a milestone-local engineering deliverable and concrete acceptance artifact.
The source defines the raised platform's height, cup clearance, and footprint; REQ_RAISED_CUP_PLATFORM is the narrower target.
Removable spouts are a cleanable-dispensing-path behavior rather than a change to the CAD deliverable, and this source is also superseded by the explicit commitment in message 144.
The freelancer commits to removable spouts, which belongs to REQ_CLEANABLE_DISPENSING_PATH rather than the system-layout and CAD artifact.
The downward-pour orientation is an independently testable spout-configuration behavior and is better assigned to REQ_SPOUT_CONFIGURATION.
The client adds retention of the CAD files as a concrete engineering-documentation obligation for future development.
This is the first target-specific implementation claim that the CAD files were saved with the project documentation.
Lighting around the bowls is an independently testable visual-design behavior represented by REQ_LED_ACCENT_LIGHTING, not a change to the CAD deliverable itself.
